findings.finding: Post-record variable-length metadata edits invalidate disk membership byte offsets if journal frames are copied without relocation.
findings.disposition: One-group bounded rewrite validates membership symbol/key order/count and relocates completion anchors, including empty/non-set anchors. GDX data offsets remain unchanged. Tests edit before/after multiple sets and dependents, then verify strict alias membership and exact record values.

findings.finding: Relaxed display-domain names are independent of strict symbols in pinned native SetDomainX/GetDomainX.
findings.disposition: Separate private display frames retain strict validation and direct alias IDs. Repeated late names serialize display precedence with strict IDs intact; bad arity/names fail explicitly. Independent native/Rust expectations check both views together.

findings.finding: Set-text node numbers are ephemeral, can be any signed integer and cannot overwrite a nonzero assignment.
findings.disposition: Sparse node frames preserve i32::MIN/MAX and slot 0, without using node values as allocation indices. Node state is excluded from GDX; fresh opens return zero. Native author/session probes and source hashes verify non-persistence.

findings.finding: Writer symbol metadata previously always emitted a false set-text flag.
findings.disposition: Accepted nonzero set-text levels now mark/serialize the real flag; alias/non-set/empty flags stay false. Native context expectations compare every flag independently of record counts and text strings.

findings.finding: Mapped/native domain callbacks require mapped ordering without losing original IDs or hiding partial output and cleanup failures.
findings.disposition: Explicit source-bound prescan/sort/dedup under existing map quotas, fixed callback pairs, acknowledgment counters and explicit cursor close before parent cleanup. Missing maps, preparation IO, callback faults, secondary cursor/parent denial and abort retry regressions pass with no implicit replay.

findings.finding: Read-session label mutation can cause stale labels or accidental source/catalog mutation.
findings.disposition: Separate bounded metadata overlay, latest exact-byte override lookup and source-checked explicit mapped join. Core Reader labels remain immutable; sessions are independent. Source file SHA256 is unchanged after every native and Rust context, and callback source-change tests are terminal.

findings.finding: Metadata replacement failures can leave original/replacement files or lose ownership during rename/reopen.
findings.disposition: Existing live-copy quota and reserved auxiliary slot charge both extents/buffers; both handles close before rename. IO/reopen/quota and lazy allocation/cleanup retry cases preserve primary errors and block publication.

findings.finding: Native UEL folding/trimming, sentinel strings and automatic expansion differ from the core exact-ID/byte contract.
findings.disposition: API-by-API inventory documents deliberate unsupported behavior and phase rules. Rust collision/owner/label/node validation remains strict; native probes are separate evidence, not weakened parity expectations.

limitations: Exact-byte labels deliberately differ from native folding/right trimming; symbol matching remains folded. New writer/override labels use existing <=63-byte quotable rules; source lookup preserves bounded short strings.

Schema identity, new registration and strict domains freeze before data. Existing UEL rename, comments, display metadata and session nodes remain editable between closed symbols; published/failed/aborted writers reject operations. Late acronym mutation remains unsupported.

Read sessions never expand catalogs, mutate source files or alter other sessions. Node state is not serialized. Caller maps remain immutable bijections; no implicit expansion, native ambiguity or unsafe sentinels are emulated.

Each explicit read overlay is a separate scratch job using a shared Reader memory root, existing six-handle allocator and journal quota half. Map/view pairs have separate explicit disk quotas. Reported context handle peak is per-job maximum, not an aggregate process FD bound.

Renames rewrite journals; overlay/history and metadata scans may be quadratic or worse. Domain callbacks explicitly prescan and sort; maximum-length queries explicitly scan. No throughput, RSS or oversized-operation qualification; task 031 retains M4 acceptance.

Mapped domain callbacks require complete observed mappings; selected/raw extraction uses existing unique_domains. Native legacy filter/error-list/callback call-state emulation and global current-symbol state are unsupported.

Caller-retained fixed-size information/callback results use caller memory. Existing std/path/control-allocation limitations remain. Drop is best effort; explicit close/abort reports retryable cleanup errors.
Native helper qualification is Linux isolated reference work. Four native Rust CI targets qualify functionality/logical accounting, not cross-platform OS memory/performance parity.
No new dependency, unsafe code, GDX/public spill format, frozen generator or golden/hash relaxation. Private journals extend typed frame tags. Tasks 030 and 031 remain pending.
